subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers fail closed on every legacy ownerless session row, or must this change include a safe migration or operator recovery path?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes persisted upgrade behavior at a plugin authorization boundary; code review can identify the defect, but maintainers must own the security-versus-compatibility policy for existing ownerless rows.

options.title: Fail closed with recovery
options.body: Reject ownerless rows, provide a documented operator or doctor recovery path, and prove fresh and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Add ownership migration
options.body: Define and test a narrow migration that assigns ownership without allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

options.title: Preserve temporary compatibility
options.body: Keep ownerless access under an explicit temporary compatibility policy with a removal plan.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with recovery
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows, provide a documented operator or doctor recovery path, and prove fresh and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history owns the projection accessor and patch transaction boundary where this policy must be implemented safely.
